plan.theme: helping mother cook dal bhat in the kitchen, in a hill village in Nepal

attempts.prompt:
You write decodable reading stories for a simple English beginner reader aged 4-10 in Nepal.

Child's name: Sita (always allowed; spell it EXACTLY like this. In Nepali you may attach case endings: Sitaले, Sitaको, Sitaलाई, Sitaमा, Sitaसँग)
Theme: helping mother cook dal bhat in the kitchen, in a hill village in Nepal
Focus units to practise often: d, m
Key words for this theme (the child can read these; use them): dad pan
Do NOT write these even though they are natural (the child cannot read them yet): mum pot

Every word in the title and story MUST come from the word bank (case-insensitive).
Use ONLY words from the word bank. No other words at all, not even small ones.

Word bank:
a am an and as at dad dads dam damp dams did dim dip dips dish in is it mad man map maps mash mat mats mid mint nap naps nip nips pad pads pan pans pat pin pins pit pits sad sand sandpit sandpits sap sat ship ships sip sips sit sits snap snaps snip snips spin spins stamp stamps stand stands tan tap taps the tin tins tip tips

Rules:
- exactly 3 short sentences, at most 5 words each. Simple, warm, coherent. Repetition is good.
- Every word at most 4 sounds long (the child's name is exempt). Prefer short words.
- A short title using the same constraints.
- Everyday Nepali child life: family, village, animals, food, school.
- No violence, fear, danger, sadness or adult themes.
- "scene": one English sentence describing a picture for the story (animals and objects, no detailed faces).
attempts.title: Dad and Sita

result.title: Dad and Sita
result.scene: Sita and her dad sit on a woven mat in a simple kitchen beside a metal cooking pan.

safety.reason: The story is simple, educational, and contains no inappropriate content for children.
